title: Tenant reconciliation and deferred-acknowledgement customer brief
body:
Summary:

This is a customer-facing draft summarizing the incident on 2029-08-20 that caused delayed acknowledgement (deferred-acknowledge) for a subset of streaming and queued inference requests and resulted in transient duplicate or delayed responses for affected tenants. We are circulating this draft for review before posting a concise statuspage update and sending tenant-specific reconciliation guidance.

Who was impacted:
- Small fraction of tenants using streaming or large-batch endpoints in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 during the incident window.
- Impact types observed: delayed response delivery (30s–10m), rare duplicate responses, and cases where client-side timeouts caused apparent 'missing' responses while our backend was still processing.

Customer-facing timeline (UTC):
- 2029-08-20 16:03 — First elevated error rates and increased broker queue depth detected by automated SLO alerts.
- 2029-08-20 16:05 — Incident channel opened. Immediate mitigation: isolated overloaded broker instance and throttled large-batch jobs.
- 2029-08-20 16:07 — Partial prefix-KV cache eviction observed; some model shards refreshed.
- 2029-08-20 16:11 — We deployed a rate-limiting hotfix (rollback threshold adjustment) to reduce backpressure; duplicate delivery symptoms reduced.
- 2029-08-20 16:35 — Queue depths returned to normal; streaming latencies stabilized for most tenants.
- 2029-08-20 18:00 — Full verification pass completed; statuspage update authored for 18:15 publication.

Root cause (high-level):
- A combination of message broker backpressure and an unexpected race in our deferred-acknowledgement path caused some requests to remain in a pending-ack state longer than intended. When clients retried or when internal replay logic triggered, a small percentage of requests were processed twice or delivered after consumer timeouts.
- Contributing factors: sudden workload spike from a customer-side job pattern + kernel-level delay during a shard snapshot that increased per-request handling time and prevented timely ack processing.

What we did (immediate mitigations):
- Isolated and restarted the impacted broker instance to clear stuck inflight message batches.
- Applied temporary throttle rules on large-batch endpoints and streaming consumers to contain queue growth.
- Tweaked deferred-ack timeouts and improved health-check routing to avoid routing new requests to the affected shard until cache warmup completed.
- Contacted customers with high-volume patterns directly via SEs to coordinate replays.

What we are doing (short-term & next steps):
- Short-term (next 72 hours):
  - Push monitoring rule changes to alert earlier on deferred-ack backlog and per-tenant in-queue age.
  - Publish a tenant-specific replay guide and evidence package so customers can safely reconcile missing or duplicate results.
  - Provide an opt-in replay window appliance for enterprise tenants who request assistance; SREs will run replays into a dry-run verification mode first.
- Medium-term (1–4 weeks):
  - Fix the race in the deferred-ack path and improve idempotency metadata propagation so duplicates are detected and suppressed safely at delivery time.
  - Harden broker snapshot/eviction to avoid latency spikes during shard snapshots.
  - Add per-tenant circuit breaker thresholds that scale more conservatively for high-burst patterns.
- Long-term (>4 weeks):
  - Introduce stronger client-visible delivery guarantees with optional dedup token support and documented replay semantics.

Customer actions and guidance (concise):
- If you observed missing responses: do not reprocess requests indiscriminately. Contact support with a request for an evidence package (see below) so we can validate which requests were processed and help you replay only missing inputs.
- If you observed duplicates: identify duplicate request IDs (if you use request-id headers) and follow dedup guidance in our replay doc. If you do not send request IDs, our SRE team can help deduplicate on the backend for enterprise tenants.
- For self-serve reconciliations: follow the steps in the linked replay guide (we will publish an updated appendix) — start with a dry-run using a small sample, validate outputs, then run full replay with dedup tokens.

Evidence package and how to request it:
- Evidence package contents (available on request): per-request processing timeline, broker offsets, delivery attempts, and server-side logs that reference request ids and tenant ids.
- To request: open a support ticket referencing OPS-5421 or reply to your SE contact. For enterprise customers, include a preferred time window for coordinated replay (we recommend off-peak hours).

SLA and credits:
- We are reviewing affected tenant lists and will propose SLO crediting where our internal verification shows measurable customer impact consistent with our SLA policy. If you believe your usage met the impact conditions, please flag the support ticket and include traffic samples.

How we will communicate updates:
- Short post to status.redwood.ai at 2029-08-21 18:15 UTC with a concise incident summary and link to this reconciliation guidance.
- Customer-success will send tenant-specific notes to known impacted customers within 24 hours (SEs copied).
- A more detailed public postmortem will be published to Confluence (linked above) after full RCA is complete (~2 weeks).

Draft status and asks for reviewers:
- This is a customer-ready draft but marked DRAFT while engineering signs off on the RCA wording and SRE confirms replay steps are operational.
- Asks: eng-SRE and applied-ml to confirm the short-term mitigation wording and that the evidence package fields are accurate; SEs to review suggested customer language for clarity and tone.

Appendix (tech notes for reviewers):
- Observed metrics: peak in-queue age to 12m for affected broker partitions; deferred-ack counter spiked 23x baseline.
- Key logs: see linked GitHub PR and OPS ticket for redacted examples.
- Temporary config: rollback of deferred-ack threshold set to 8s -> 3s at 2029-08-20 16:11 UTC; will be reverted once idempotency protections are in place.

Contact:
- Customer-success lead: Sophie Chen (sophie@redwood.ai)
- On-call SRE: Ethan Morales
- For enterprise coordination: Priya Kapoor (solutions)
